local_facts.title: A crash report can still leave a separate 10-day DMV task
local_facts.claim: California DMV requires an SR-1 within 10 days when a crash causes any injury or death, or more than $1,000 in property damage; it is separate from a police, CHP, or insurance report.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A Modesto collision file can have a CHP or police report and still carry an independent DMV reporting deadline.

local_facts.title: The familiar 15/30/5 shorthand is not the current floor
local_facts.claim: California raised standard auto-policy minimum liability limits as policies renewed beginning January 1, 2025, from $15,000/$30,000/$5,000 to $30,000/$60,000/$15,000.
local_facts.why_it_matters: The crash and policy-renewal dates affect which limits are relevant. A minimum limit is not a measure of the full loss.

local_facts.title: Stanislaus County’s traffic-injury volume makes early evidence practical
local_facts.claim: The California Office of Traffic Safety recorded 4,679 people killed or injured in Stanislaus County traffic collisions in 2023, including 389 fatal-and-injury hit-and-run collisions.
local_facts.why_it_matters: In a county with this volume of serious crash events, report requests, camera preservation, witness details, and insurance records need early attention.

pricing.table_head: What California fixes for a Stanislaus County injury claim, and where the caps really apply

anchors.label: Statutory percentage for a traffic collision claim
anchors.detail: The State Bar rule bars an unconscionable or illegal fee, and the fee statute for injury contracts requires the contract to say the rate is negotiable.

anchors.label: Medical negligence ceiling, before a filing
anchors.detail: California's only numeric fee ceiling reaches claims against health care providers, and it drops to this level when the release is signed before anything is filed.

anchors.label: First paper, unlimited civil case
anchors.detail: Due from the plaintiff when a case worth more than $35,000 is filed, and again from every other party that files a first paper.
anchors.source_name: Statewide Civil Fee Schedule, eff. Jan. 1, 2026 (Gov. Code 70611)

anchors.label: Advance jury fee
anchors.detail: A nonrefundable deposit required to keep the right to a jury, with daily jury deposits set separately by the court once trial begins.
anchors.source_name: Cal. Code Civ. Proc. 631(b), 2026 fee schedule

fee_rows.stage: Share of a vehicle injury recovery
fee_rows.note: Only the unconscionable-or-illegal standard applies. The legislature wrote percentage limits for medical negligence claims and left driving cases out.

fee_rows.stage: What the contract must tell the client
fee_rows.note: The statute requires that sentence whenever the medical negligence limits do not apply, plus a duplicate signed copy handed over at signing.

fee_rows.stage: Claim against a health care provider
fee_rows.note: Measured on the net sum after costs, and a higher share needs a motion showing good cause to the court or arbitrator.

fee_rows.stage: Filing in Stanislaus County Superior Court
fee_rows.note: Charged on the complaint in an unlimited civil case and on each other party's first paper, which is why defense answers add up.
Deposited in advance under the code, then daily jury deposits are set by the court for each day the panel sits.
One charge covers all plaintiffs, then each defendant owes the same, with a total of $18,000 for the whole case.
